title: New trombonist replaces Edwards, and unreleased records
summary: He explains how Emil learned Edwards's parts after Edwards was drafted and mentions two unreleased Victor records.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I'm sorry, I didn't get anything about the trombone player.

Oh, yes. Edwards was drafted around, in the middle, almost in fall. We came to New Orleans to get a trombone player. Emil played connet. He had been with several bands up to Chicago. And they were unsuccessful. He came back to New Orleans to play. And when we came back here to look for a trombone player, Spobora met Emil and told him, ask him if he knew a good trombone player. He said, well, how about give me a chance? Emil had started to change it to trombone. He said, all right. We went to Shields' house. Shields lived in, which is now a colored neighborhood today, in Surrey and Willop. And we sat down in there with the phonograph record. We played along with this man here, which is a Christian. Until they learned all the parts that Edwards could play. And then it was almost four weeks. Went back to Risenwebers to resume our place. And you'll have notice in there, return of the Dixieland Jazz band. Could have been somewhere in September the 6th or 7th, that he played. On October the 8th, he played on the Winter Garden with us. First time Amy had played. First time any trombone player played this show. And he played a series of shows with us before we went off. That was the new trombone player. His parts was copied from Edwards' trombone part. Now you don't have to believe me to take the records that Emil played. Take the records that Edwards played and you'll see that he's got the trombone parts of Edwards.
Did he make any records in this country with him, Emil?
He made two records with us, Satanic Blues and Lass's Candy, which was never put out by Victor. Those are the records we made before we went to London, England. And they never were released.
